question: Who is held to be the supreme guru, and on what basis?
premises: Someone knows in essence or reality.
That person is regarded as a guru.
The guruship so attained is supreme.
inference: Whoever knows in essence is held to be the supreme guru.
uncertainties: tattvena reads as instrumental of means (by essence) but an adverbial sense (essentially) is possible; left open.
Whether paramo mataḥ closes this verse or opens the next unit is decided by the passage tiling, not this verse alone.
plain_english: Whoever knows in essence is held to be the supreme guru.
